findings.scope: ## Goals and Non-Goals vs ## Acceptance criteria
findings.text: AC-20 (import boundary) and AC-21 (documents) are cited by no goal, though every other AC from AC-10 to AC-19 is traced to a G-n.

The second-level headings mix title case ("Goals and Non-Goals", "Open Questions", "Critical User Journeys", "Non-Functional Requirements") with sentence case ("Acceptance criteria", "Risks and rollback").
Nine test files, each mapped to its ACs, are packed into one run-on paragraph separated by semicolons where a list or table would make the mapping from file to AC readable.

Fixed output texts are written in plain quotes ("run wizardingcode-mem update for the commands", "not a release redirect") where every other fixed text in the document is in code spans, so it is unclear whether these are exact strings.
Design 1 ties its bullets to ACs inline (AC-19, AC-20), but Designs 2 and 3 cite none, so the links between design and criteria are uneven.

"one request a day to github.com" and "One request a day per data directory while turns end; none otherwise" are false under the spec's own design: after failures the backoff retries at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours (up to six requests in a day), and `wizardingcode-mem update` asks on every run, so the README would make a claim about network use that the product breaks.
findings.reason: Right: with the backoff the README claim of one request a day was false. The backoff becomes flat (one hour after a failure, 24 hours after a success) and the README and the requirements say what is true: at most one request a day while checks succeed, at most one an hour while they fail, plus one for each wizardingcode-mem update typed.

findings.text: "is a pure function that answers `none`, `stage` or `hand-over` candidates: `none` unless this process is a compiled binary; whose real path … is not the staged binary's; …" has broken grammar and does not say whether `decide` compares versions (it takes `staged`, yet "reconcile then reads the staged binary's version"), so an implementer cannot tell what `decide` returns, or which of the conditions are guards and which are outcomes.
findings.reason: Right: the paragraph is rewritten. decide takes the guards and answers skip or compare; it compares no version. reconcile reads the staged version and chooses stage, hand over or nothing.

findings.text: "within a day or two of use after a release" is not measurable; the design gives the bound (a turn ending more than 24 hours after the last check), so the goal should state it.

"the product has downloaded and changed nothing" conflicts with G-3 and J-5, where `status` from a newer channel copy stages that copy and the check writes `update.json`; the claim needs its scope ("nothing because of the notice").

"carries nothing about the machine" is an absolute claim that Risks qualify ("tells github.com that an address runs the product"); say what the request leaves out (version, platform, paths, projects), as Design 1 does, and do not make the absolute claim.

"within a day a client that already runs 0.10.0 reads …" holds only while turns end and checks succeed; a client in backoff, or one where no turn ends, sees it later. The runbook line in Design 4 ("within about a day") carries the same unstated condition.
"AC-1 to AC-9 were retired when the leads' returns changed their texts" is process jargon that means nothing to a reader without the session ("the engine's", "leads' returns").
"the four blockers" is never listed in this spec, so a reader writing ADR 0030 or the findings row has to go to `concepts_brief.md` to learn what they are.
"a hold signal" and "its five readers" are used undefined; the reader cannot tell what signal or which five readers are meant.
"A reconciled command therefore runs the staged binary's `--version` at most twice" does not follow from the paragraph about temporary file names it closes; the "therefore" has no premise there.
it repeats the closing sentence of Design 3 (at most twice, 10 seconds each) and adds no risk or answer of its own.
a single sentence of about 120 words packs the decision point, the leaf module, its exports, its import limits and testability together; the reader has to parse it several times to find the rule.
`<age>` is used in every line ("checked 2 h ago", "3 h ago" in the journeys), but its format (units, rounding, "just now") is never stated, so the exact text AC-14 tests is not fully defined.

Phase 3 has `status`, `doctor` and the report's callers read `staged` with `stagedVersion`, but `stagedVersion` is only exported (with its limit) in Phase 4, so Phase 3 does not typecheck as ordered and the phases are not each buildable.
findings.reason: Right: the export of stagedVersion and the staged path helper move to the first phase, so each phase typechecks.

findings.text: `agoLabel` is a private function in src/doctor/checks.ts:178, a file that imports src/store, src/modules and src/sync and that itself imports src/status/report.ts; "moves to or is imported from where it lives" leaves the choice open, and importing it would create a cycle (checks → status/report → update/report → checks) and pull the store into src/update; an exported `ago(now, at)` that clamps negative ages already exists in src/status/report.ts:151 and the plan does not mention it (the Files table also calls it `ageLabel`).

findings.text: `StatusReport.update` is defined as the report without `lines`, yet `formatStatus(report)` must print the lines and the commands when `out`; the plan does not say where `formatStatus` gets `lines` and `out`, whether `update` is required or optional on `StatusReport` (src/ui/server.ts also calls `statusReport`), or that status.ts assigns it after `statusReport` returns.

findings.text: "in the `catch`, the version line and the update lines are printed on standard output" says nothing about `--json`; as written, `status --json` against a broken store writes plain text to stdout, and the shape for that case is not decided.
findings.reason: Right: with --json and a store that cannot be opened, status prints one JSON object {version, update, error} on standard output and exits 1; without --json the version line and the update lines, then the error on standard error.

findings.text: J-4 requires that when the check is off, `update` "prints that the check is off and how to turn it on"; the plan only says it prints the report's lines (`update: off (WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE)`), with no text for how to turn it on and no exit code for off / off-unknown.
findings.reason: Right: with the check off, update prints the off line and the sentence: set WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE=check in <data dir>/env to turn it on, prints no commands, and exits 0.

findings.text: the rule is not given for a state that has `attemptAt` but neither `checkedAt` nor `failedAt` (the first request killed mid-flight), or `failures > 0` with `failedAt` null after the future-time reset; a reader can make `due` return false forever and the client never checks again; the plan also does not say how "after a success" is told from "after a failure" (`failures > 0` or `failedAt > checkedAt`).
findings.reason: Right: due is restated as total: no state, or no checkedAt and no failedAt, is due once 60 seconds have passed since attemptAt (or at once when attemptAt is null or in the future); the last event is a failure when failedAt is a number and checkedAt is null or earlier; then one hour after failedAt, else 24 hours after checkedAt.

findings.text: the sentence says the summary is `1 warning.`, then says the count is not asserted because other checks may warn, then switches to `runChecks` in-process; the assertion to write for AC-15's "exit code stays 0 with that warning alone" cannot be read from it.

the sentence "(with a spy on `renameSync` through a source that records the temporary name, or by listing the folder from a `copyFileSync` wrapper is not available)" is garbled; only the planted-link assertion that follows can be built.
the plan does not say whether `known: null` counts as "given" (skip the read, treat as unreadable) or as absent.

the printed format of `CHANNEL_COMMANDS` in `status` and `update` (a heading, indentation, channel labels) is not given, and neither are the signatures of `updateLine` and `agentsLine`, which the Files table lists.

findings.text: `StatusReport` gains `update`, but the plan does not say whether `statusReport()` computes it or the field is optional and only `status.ts` fills it (as with `history?`). `statusReport` also serves the viewer's `/api/status` (src/ui/server.ts:767) and about 30 test call sites. findings.text: `updateReport` needs `running`, `staged`, `stagedPath` and `isStaged`, but the doctor check is described as built "from `context.dataDir`, `context.now` and `context.env`" only. Nothing says the check spawns `stagedVersion` or how it computes `isStaged` (realpath of `process.execPath`). `runChecks`' contract ("Looks, and changes nothing", checks.ts:1076) and its in-process tests are affected.

findings.scope: Phase 2 line-1 order vs Phase 3 `update` command
findings.text: Line 1 puts `ci` before any state, so `wizardingcode-mem update` run in CI makes its forced request (the plan allows force in mode `ci`) and then prints "update: not checked in CI". That contradicts what it just did and contradicts spec J-4 and Design 2 ("in CI it checks").
findings.reason: Right: the report takes checked, true when this call made a request; line 1 is not checked in CI only when the mode is ci and nothing was asked, so update in CI prints what it found.

findings.text: Spec J-4 says that with the check off, `update` "prints that the check is off and how to turn it on". The plan defines no such sentence (the only off text is `update: off (WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE)`). It also does not say whether the four channel commands are printed when off.
findings.reason: Right, same as readiness-1.9-6: the sentence that says how to turn the check on, no commands, exit 0.

findings.text: The data directory is never created (no `mkdirSync`). A forced `update`, or a `distill` check, on a machine with no `<data dir>` yet throws ENOENT. In `update`, nothing catches it, so main.ts:96 prints a raw error and exits 1. The plan also skips the existing `writeFileAtomic` (src/util/atomic-write.ts) without saying why.
findings.reason: Right: writeState creates the data directory (mode 0700) before writing, through writeFileAtomic; update catches a write failure and prints one sentence.

findings.text: On Windows `process.getuid` is undefined, so `uid` is null, while `lstat().uid` is 0. The rule "binOwner is a number other than uid" then always answers `none`, so Windows channel copies silently never reconcile; the plan does not say whether that is intended. On POSIX, `getuid` is the real uid while the spec says "the effective user" (`geteuid`).
findings.reason: Right, same as design-1.7-4: decide answers none on win32, stated; on POSIX the effective user id (geteuid) is used.

findings.text: `process.env.WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE ??= "off"` keeps a developer's shell export of `check`. Every hook-spawned `distill` in the suite would then make real github.com requests, against G-2 ("never made by the project's own tests"). The preload already deletes other behaviour variables from the shell for this reason (`WIZARDINGCODE_MODULES`, tests/preload.ts:40). Separately, `spawnCli` (tests/helpers/cli.ts:52) inherits nothing, and the plan only adds a comment there rather than any guard.
findings.reason: Right: the preload sets the key to off unconditionally, as it drops other behaviour variables from the shell, and a test that wants the check sets it for itself; the boundary test asserts it.

findings.text: "exported from `check.ts`'s sibling so both use one" does not say which file exports it, and neither Files row lists `PLAIN`.
Adding `update` to `Settings` breaks the whole-object `toEqual` defaults test at tests/unit/settings.test.ts:27-45, and the plan's list of settings.test.ts changes does not name it.

The sentence "(with a spy on `renameSync` … or by listing the folder from a `copyFileSync` wrapper is not available)" is garbled, and it leaves the choice of method open before settling on the planted link. The plan also does not say what `stageBinary` returns when `known` is newer (presumably `kept: known`).

The plan runs `rmSync(…, { force: true })` and then a plain `copyFileSync`, which still follows a link planted between the two calls. Spec Design 3 says the file is "never written through a link"; `fs.constants.COPYFILE_EXCL` would close that gap.

Bun's `spawnSync` `exitCode` can be null (killed by a signal), and the plan does not keep install's current `?? 1` (install.ts:250). The spawn-failure text also changes from `wizardingcode-mem install: could not run` to `wizardingcode-mem: could not run` without saying so.

`install` is not reconciled, so the `WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_HANDED=1` it now passes to the handed-over staged `install` is never deleted from that child's environment. That is against spec Design 3's "removed from the environment the handed-over command gives its own children".

The plan never says how the data directory is found (`defaultDataDir()` or `resolvePaths`). It also leaves `failedAt`-later-than-`checkedAt` undefined when `checkedAt` is null, and `status --json` output in the catch path unspecified.
It says the summary is `1 warning.` and then says the count is asserted elsewhere through `runChecks`. The two statements contradict each other about what the test actually asserts.

The Alternatives never weigh the simplest answer to Problem 3: the older copy only tells, the same way D-3 makes the newer copy only tell (a second line naming the staged path, or the SchemaTooNewError text naming `<path> doctor`). The hand-over brings `decide` with its root and owner rules, `WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_HANDED`, the `reconciled.ts` leaf, `COMMAND_NAMES`, a new Limit ("runs the staged file") and an e2e suite. Without that comparison a reader cannot tell whether running a binary from the data directory on every `status`/`doctor`/`update`/`ui` is worth its cost over a one-line notice.
findings.reason: Right that the comparison was missing. The Alternatives now weigh an older copy that only tells: it would leave the person with a schema error on the command they typed to diagnose, and install already hands over, so the mechanism exists. The hand-over stays (the author's D-1, untouched by D-3), with its cost stated: decide, the guard variable, the leaf, and an e2e.

findings.text: `failures` is counted, validated, tested ("a failure … counts") and reset, but nothing reads it: `due` uses a flat hour, and neither the lines nor the report show it. It is left over from the rejected 1-2-4-…-24 h backoff and could be dropped.

findings.scope: spec.md Design 1 "The request" and AC-10 vs plan.md Phase 2 `latestRelease`
findings.text: The spec says `Location` is "matched whole", but the plan compares it "after lower-casing the owner and repository on both sides". The two disagree on whether a `Location` whose letter case differs from the constant passes. The probe shows github.com echoes the request's case, so the exact match the spec states is enough.

The spec checks the owner of `<data dir>/bin` "or, when it does not exist, its nearest existing parent", but the plan uses `binOwner` null when `bin` is missing. The plan's version is enough because with no `bin` there is nothing to hand over to, so the spec's nearest-parent rule is over-built and the two should say the same thing.
The spec says `update` "exits 1 only when its check failed", but the plan also exits 1 when the state cannot be written ("could not record the check").
The parameter that says whether this call asked is named `checked` in the spec's `updateReport` signature and `asked` in the plan's.
The `StagedFacts` interface has no `exists`, but the prose below it adds `exists: boolean`. The test line promises `agentsLine` "in its five cases" and then lists six.

`stagedFacts` always runs the staged binary's `--version`, even when `isSelf` is true and the answer is already `pkg.version`. So every `status` and `doctor` typed through the staged binary or a hook-run path starts itself once for no reason.

`ago` moves to `src/util/` for reuse, but `agoLabel` in `src/doctor/checks.ts:178` does the same job and stays. The new `update` check in that same file will then use one form and the `backups` check the other.

findings.scope: spec.md Design 1 and 3 (`due` order, regex digit limits, `decide`/`handOver` signatures)
findings.text: The spec holds algorithm- and signature-level detail that the plan repeats. Keeping two copies is why F-3, F-4 and F-6 have already drifted apart. The spec could state the rules and leave the step order and signatures to the plan.

The full list of commands in a leaf, with `main.ts`'s table typed by it, exists mainly so that a test can check `reconciles` is true for exactly four names. A check of `RECONCILED` and the `ui --auto` case would cover the same rule without a second list of commands to keep in sync.

findings.scope: Design 2, table row order ("the last event is a failure" before "the latest is higher") and the doctor bullet
findings.text: once a check has recorded a newer release, any later failed check (a flaky network, a captive portal, a corporate block on github.com, a 429) changes `status` to "could not check …; last known 0.10.0", leaves out the commands and turns `doctor`'s `update` check from `warn` to `ok`; under hourly retries the notice flips on and off, and on a network that keeps failing it never comes back, so G-1 fails exactly where people are least likely to notice a release by other means.
findings.reason: Right: a release already found stays announced. When the latest known is higher than the current version, line 1 is the is-out line whatever the last event, with the failure appended (last check failed: reason, age); doctor stays warn and status keeps the commands.

findings.scope: Design 1 "The mode" with J-3 and the README bullet
findings.text: the mode comes from the process's own environment, so `status` typed in a shell that exports `WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE=off` (or `CI`) prints `update: off`, while the `distill` that the agent's hooks start (often from a GUI-launched agent that does not inherit that shell's environment) still sends the request; for a privacy switch the report can say "off" while requests are going out, and the spec neither names this nor makes `<data dir>/env` the documented way to turn it off.
findings.reason: Right: the mode is read by each process from its own environment and the file, so a shell export does not reach a hook started elsewhere. The documented way to turn the check off is the file <data dir>/env, which every process reads; the off line says where the value came from (this command's environment, or the file), and when it came from the environment it adds that other processes may not see it.

findings.text: the hand-over runs only in a copy that already contains this item, so every channel copy shipped before it (0.8.x Homebrew and downloaded binaries) still fails with `SchemaTooNewError` against a store a newer staged binary migrated; the first copies that benefit are those released after this item, and neither Limits nor Risks says so, which overstates what the item fixes.
findings.reason: Right: stated in Limits and in the README's install section: the hand-over exists only in copies that carry this item; an older channel copy still fails against a migrated store.

findings.text: the fixed hint "set WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE=check in <data dir>/env to turn it on" does nothing when the `off` came from the environment, which wins over the file; the line does not say where the value came from.

`attemptAt` is written before the request, so in a data directory that cannot be written the check throws every time and is only logged, and `status` stays at "not checked yet" with no reason; the spec does not name this case.

the probe says it did not test Bun's `fetch` with `redirect: "manual"` inside a compiled binary, which is what ships; this can be checked by building, but it is in neither Risks nor an acceptance criterion (the AC-18 e2e covers the hand-over, not the request).

`stagedVersion` is said to be "remembered for the process" but the spec does not say what key it is remembered by, and `stageBinary` calls it too; it should be kept by path so a later read cannot get a stale answer. Even when this process is the staged binary, `status` from it still spawns its own `--version` (up to 10 s), which the NFR does not count.
it says `checkForRelease` makes no request "when `CI` is set" with no exception, while Design 1 and AC-25 make a forced `update` ask in CI; the two criteria read as contradicting each other.

how long the work takes and what the midway check is are not stated; "one item and one pull request" covers cost, and the only check of success named is the author reading `update` on the first release after the merge.

AC-23 cites G-3, but G-3 cites only AC-26, so the goal-to-criterion links do not match both ways. AC-23 tests `reconciles` and `decide`, which belong to the hand-over (G-4), not the telling (G-3), so the G-3 citation is probably wrong.
A blank line between AC-19 and AC-21 splits the criteria list into two lists, or makes it a loose list. No other item in the list has this gap.

This level-3 heading sits under `## Design` next to the numbered subsections 1 to 4, but it is not numbered and holds limits and failure modes. The rubric puts those under risks. `## Risks and rollback` does not point to it, so the limits are split across two sections.

The headings differ from the rubric's section names ("Proposed architecture", "Alternatives considered", "Risks and mitigations"). The rubric names no Acceptance criteria section, and this one sits between Alternatives and Risks.
About a dozen rejected options are written as one dense paragraph with no list items, so the options and the reason for rejecting each are hard to tell apart and check.
Nothing says how long the work will take. The cost (question 6) is answered only by "one item and one pull request" in the non-functional requirements.
